answer: Priced identity creation resists sybils: every new agent must complete a fresh, verifiable computation tied to its key before it can transact, and each identity is rate-limited. It is like quarrying marble — one block is cheap, but a thousand blocks cost a thousand times the work, so cloning identities is not free. Reputation then accrues only from sustained useful work, as saffron gains value only after a slow harvest, not by calling shale a spice. An attacker can afford a few identities, but flooding the market means paying the full cost for every fake, again and again.
